56790-the-travels-of-fuzz-and-buzz:
The Travels of Fuzz and Buzz is a tale of two young field mice. Geraldine Mockler wrote it for the young, with plates by Pearse. Fuzz and Buzz are the boy mouse and girl mouse of a wood home. Their sire is a wise mouse who stores food for the cold months.

Field mice feast in spring and fall, but the frost is hard on them. Nuts and fruit are gone, and a poor store means lean weeks of want. The first part tells of the sire's fall and the young ones' fright. A water rat plays hide and seek with an owl in the next part. A small bird brings bad news to the two young mice in time. They save a grey fur dame in the last of the listed parts. The tale is warm, plain, and made to be read to the young.
74145-radio-razz:
Jack Woodford's Radio Razz opens in old Doc Edwards's radio store, where the narrator likes to hang around in the evenings. He owns a five-tube set of his own. He comes for the selling, not the sets.

The Doctor's title comes from his days as a veterinary surgeon. At heart he was never a vet, the narrator says, but a horse trader. When horses fell so low that people saved the last specimens for zoos, Edwards turned to radio. He will not stock a new set without marking it secondhand, and no set in the shop carries a price tag. The story is a portrait of American salesmanship changing its stock.
